actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is the implementation of the paper One Policy to Run Them All: an End-to-end Learning Approach to Multi-Embodiment Locomotion
The requirements pin mujoco 3.1.3
The multi-robot module defines create_env(config), the environment factory
AnymalB is registered in the ROBOTS list
AnymalB is a gymnasium.Env subclass
AnymalB stores twelve nominal joint positions, twelve max_joint_velocities values of 15.0 and an initial_drop_height of 0.5
AnymalB loads the MJCF with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path and then overwrites model.opt.timestep with the timestep of its configuration
The action-space size starts at model.nu and is replaced by multi_robot_max_action_size when that value is not -1; its Box has infinite lower and upper bounds
AnymalB.reset replaces the model state with the qpos and qvel of its initial-state function
AnymalB.step runs the action through the control function's process_action, writes the resulting torques to data.ctrl and calls mujoco.mj_step for nr_substeps
The shipped anymal_b configuration sets timestep 0.005 s and an episode length of 20 s
Rudin2022Control defaults to a control frequency of 50 Hz, p_gain 80, d_gain 2.0 and a scaling factor of 0.5
process_action scales the action by the scaling factor, adds the nominal joint positions and computes a PD torque from qpos[7:] and qvel[6:]
The default initial state puts the base at the initial drop height plus the terrain centre height and the twelve joints at their nominal positions
The MJCF root element names the model anymal_b
The model uses radians, resolves its meshes from assets/ and enables autolimits
The model's option element selects the pyramidal cone and impratio 100
The default joint is a hinge with damping 1, frictionloss 0.1 and range -3.14 to 3.14
The default motor is ctrllimited with ctrlrange -40.0 to 40.0
The world contains a plane floor and a trunk body at 0 0 0 that carries the free joint
The actuator section has twelve motor actuators, one per leg joint from LF_HAA to RH_KFE
The home keyframe holds 19 qpos values with the base at height 0.5 and the listed joint positions

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates a fixed model deterministically on one engine version, but cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults and does not use a seed; the bridge publishes no seeded control and this package makes no determinism claim.

gaps: this package serves the bare MJCF through the MuJoCo bridge; it does not run create_env, AnymalB, RL-X or the environment's observation, reward, termination, command-sampling, domain-randomization and vectorization pipeline

the served action is the model's torque control vector (one value per motor, ctrlrange -40 to 40); AnymalB.step instead takes twelve joint-position offsets, scales them by 0.5 and converts them to torques with the Rudin2022 PD controller before writing data.ctrl

a reset runs mj_resetData and restores the compiled model defaults (base at 0 0 0, all joints at zero); AnymalB.reset places the trunk at initial_drop_height plus the terrain centre height (0.5 m) and the joints at the nominal pose

the MJCF states no <option timestep>, so the served step is MuJoCo's 0.002 s default; AnymalB overwrites the model timestep with the 0.005 s configuration value and integrates four substeps per 50 Hz control step

the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the MJCF for the free base, the twelve hinge joints, the twelve motors and their default ctrlrange, then gives each actuated hinge a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value and holds the free base where the model puts it; it computes no inertia, torque, gravity, contact, friction, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory
the stand-in loads no OBJ mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact; the model's floor, geometry and contact excludes are not applied
the fake exposes no mj_getState/mj_setState, so its snapshots use the bridge's basic profile; the real engine has the full integration-state codec, which this package did not run
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine, and the real sim path (a backend name backends does not list) was not run
no physical ANYmal B is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the served model state, including the last controls, is kept and stays readable. A later explicit step without action reuses those controls
